staff.name: Antoine Bourassa
staff.basis: The staffing model puts 1 of this role in a dry-goods store at the typical band and 2 at the high end, on directory_1839. The counting-house clerk is the one role the directory counts in bulk — 152 of them, the largest single trade in the 1839 list after the carpenters — and the printed forms name their houses outright ('clerk stiles burton'). A young man boarding with his employer or over the store is the ordinary arrangement; half is this model's reading of 'often', and it is a reading. This person is a reconstructed resident of the trade with no workplace of their own; the house is one the business layer already holds, and this row points at it rather than raising anything. Seated by tools/seat_reconstructed_trades_1835.py (T-1433) off 1835_business_staffing_model#dry_goods_store.clerk; carried onto this record by tools/staff_the_houses_1835.py (T-1462).
staff.replaceable_by: a source naming where this person worked, which retires the draw

hands.why_not_drawn: The reconstructed seating had nobody of this trade left to seat here. A source naming a hand at this house would write one in, and T-1448's mint order is the count of what the town still owes it.

staffing.basis: the 1835 business staffing model's band for this class, with the reconstructed seats T-1433 put in this house marked drawn

shortfall.statement: The staffing model puts 1 hand(s) about this kind of house at its typical band and this house carries 1. It is at its band.
shortfall.counted_here: the reconstructed hands this overlay seats. A hand a SOURCE names carries its own citation in staff[] and is counted by the attested join, not by this.
shortfall.replaceable_by: a source naming a hand at this house, which retires the seat it replaces, or the mint T-1448 ordered, which draws the rest

locations.basis: The register resolved no place for this house at the scene date.
locations.limit_reason: No street the model holds. The anchor "P. Pruyne & Co's store" names nothing the committed town holds.

dates.basis: No opening is announced. The first printing, 1834-09-03, is the bound: the house was trading by then and the record does not say when it began. A dissolution is printed after the scene date (chicago_democrat_1835_07_22#c007, chicago_democrat_1835_07_29#c010), so the house is closed at the last issue that carries it.

proprietor_community.basis: The 3 keeper(s) this record names and the resident layer holds a card for all read yankee: Chas. L. Bristol (yankee), John Hale (yankee), Wm. Hogue (yankee). A house is not its keeper, so the reading is an inference about the house and is capped there.

replaceable_by: A directory, a deed or a later reading that names this house's premises, its staff or its dates more exactly than the newspapers do.
